meta.title: Legonizer · Turn a 3D city model into a brick model
meta.description: Turn a 3D city model into a model of white bricks you can build, project urban data on and discuss around. Free, in your browser, with parts list, instructions and shopping lists.

hero.headline: From a 3D city model to a brick model you can build, project on and discuss around.
hero.lead: Turn your 3D city data into white bricks, with the parts to buy, step-by-step instructions and a projection layer.
hero.posterAlt: A white brick model of the Part-Dieu district on a table. A projector on a mast colours some buildings green, red and yellow to show what was built, demolished or modified, and projects a picture next to the model. Three people stand around the table; one holds a numeric keypad. A screen on the mast shows a timeline.

what.title: A brick model of your city, ready to build
what.body: The Legonizer turns a 3D model of a city into a model made of white bricks on square baseplates of 32 × 32 studs. It gives you everything you need to build it: the list of bricks to buy, step-by-step building instructions and a projection layer for your projector.
what.imageModelAlt: A district built with white bricks on grey baseplates.
what.imageProjectionAlt: Coloured data projected onto a white brick model.
what.imageScreenAlt: A screen showing the same district in 3D.

why.title: Why bricks, and why project on them?
why.intro: A physical model brings people around one table. A digital model can show data, change and time. An augmented model combines both: a projector shows urban data on the bricks while a screen shows the 3D city.

together.title: Around one table
together.body: Everyone looks at the same model and can point at it. It is easier to talk about a place together.

tangible.title: You can touch it
tangible.body: People walk around the model, lean in and recognise their street, even if they don't read maps.

white.title: White bricks make a screen
white.body: The projector lights up the white bricks with building uses, green spaces or tram lines, right where they are.

modular.title: Modular, reusable, playful
modular.body: Take it apart and build another district, or the same one at another scale. Building it together is part of the fun.

import.title: 1. Import a 3D city model
import.body: Use our Part-Dieu demo or your own file: 3D Tiles, glTF, OBJ or CityJSON. Everything stays on your computer.

area.title: 2. Choose the area and the scale
area.body: Draw the district you want and see how big it will be on the table before you start.

build.title: 3. Build it, project on it
build.body: Get the parts list, step-by-step instructions, shopping lists and the projection layer.

shelf.title: A brick shelf
shelf.body: Every brick you need, drawn to scale, with quantities and part numbers.

instructions.title: 3D instructions
instructions.body: Plate by plate, layer by layer. Works on a phone at the table.

pdf.title: A printable guide
pdf.body: A map of the plates, a height grid and a diagram for every layer.

shop.title: Shopping lists
shop.body: Ready to import on BrickLink or Rebrickable.

projection.title: A projection layer
projection.body: A top view of your model to line up the projector and draw your own data layers.

data.title: Data files
data.body: The height of every stud (CSV), a 3D model for LDraw tools and a project file to start again later.

facilitators.title: Workshop facilitators and museums
facilitators.body: Build a district for a public workshop, an exhibition or a neighbourhood project centre.

planners.title: Urban planners and researchers
planners.body: Make a model of a precise area at a precise scale, with settings you can reproduce.

teachers.title: Teachers, students and makers
teachers.body: Learn about your city by building it, starting from a ready-made demo.

useCase.title: Use case: a workshop on Part-Dieu
useCase.intro: Part-Dieu is Lyon's business district, organised around its railway station. Here is how a workshop group can use the Legonizer to talk about how it changed.

build.title: Build
build.body: The group builds the district from white bricks, one baseplate per team, following the instructions.

project.title: Project
project.body: The projector shows what each building is used for, the green spaces and the tram lines, right on the bricks.

compare.title: Compare
compare.body: The screen shows earlier versions of the district. The projector colours the buildings that changed: green for built, red for demolished, yellow for modified.

discuss.title: Discuss
discuss.body: Pictures and documents appear next to the model. A numeric keypad passes from hand to hand to switch layers and versions.

credits.title: Credits
credits.research: The Legonizer comes from research on augmented physical models of cities by C. Le Bihan Gautier, J. Delanoy and G. Gesquière, VCity team, LIRIS lab (CNRS, Université de Lyon).
credits.paperCitation: Représentation de l'évolution urbaine à travers une maquette tangible de territoires. Journées Françaises de l'Informatique Graphique (JFIG), Strasbourg, October 2024. hal-04924304.
credits.udviz: It extends the Legonizer widget of UD-Viz, the VCity team's open-source framework for urban data.
credits.data: Demo data: Métropole de Lyon open data.
credits.illustrative: The building uses, green spaces, tram line, changes and pictures shown in the animation are illustrative, not real data. The brick model is real: it comes from our own pipeline on the Part-Dieu demo data.
